sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: P.E. Analytics is a cash-rich real-estate information business with a meaningful recurring subscription franchise, alongside a weaker and more cyclical valuation-services subsidiary. The decisive strength is data renewal revenue financed partly by customer advances; the decisive risk is that announced platform expansion creates recurring payroll before its revenues are proven. This is an asset-light growth/value watchlist thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder designation. At the authenticated but stale October 9 reference of ₹187, the funded base model returns 10.04%, below the 15% hurdle, versus -8.51% bear and 23.11% bull. The base 15% hurdle reference is ₹149.98, not a live buy order. BQS 6.6 and GQS 6.9 are scoreable; IAS stays NS because full-window liquidity is not established. Better returns require profitable adoption of the new team, a lower executable price, or stronger evidenced growth, not counting proposed funding as cash.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exact issuer: P.E. Analytics Limited, PROPEQUITY, INE0KN801013, CIN L70102DL2008PLC172384, NSE SME. Older statement headers retain a U-prefix CIN, a presentation issue not a different issuer. Information cutoff 20 October 2026; intended market reference 19 October; last actual official trade 9 October at₹187. Financial scope is consolidated Indian GAAP/AS, not IndAS; FY2021 is standalone and FY2022 is partial acquisition scope. Five-year return horizon 19 October 2026–19 October 2031 uses actual days/365.25, nominal pre-tax equity hurdle 15%, INR crore and illustrative₹500000 position. Share count 10,879,904 includes the actual July allotment. High confidence on current audited statements, exactISIN and shareholding; Medium on operating economics/organic growth and forward margins; Low on executable price and full-window liquidity. G1/G2/G4 are Conditional, G3 Clear. No critical material accounting Hold is inferred from bounded presentation discrepancies, but no IAS ranking is allowed.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 primitive factors are reused without changes across BQS, GQS and IAS. BQS weights governance/moat 20% each, revenue/capital 12% each, durability/cash 10% each and balance/execution 8% each. GQS weights revenue 40%, durability 20%, earnings/capital 15% each and cash 10%. IAS uses unrounded final BQS25%, return 35%, downside 20%, price 10% and liquidity 10%. Scores use exact Decimal arithmetic and half-up one-decimal display; missing L is not replaced by 5 or treated as failed business quality. No governance, survival or destructive-cash ceiling applies. IAS mathematical bounds describe missing-factor uncertainty only and do not become a point score or executable setup. Factors and exact contributions are reproduced below; each records evidence, contrary facts, confidence and change triggers.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Prop Equity monetizes primary property data through subscription access and customized research, largely for real-estate developers, banks, investment institutions and other professional users in India. Annual fees vary with geography/vertical access; repeated research and updating are ongoing service costs, not a software licence with zero maintenance. FY26 subscription₹29.006 cr plus research₹1.4081 cr represent about 65% of group operating revenue. Propedge,80%-owned since January 2022, contributes property valuation services₹16.4132 cr, about 35%; inspections and personnel make this a different, more service-intensive economic model. New 65%-owned Tech and Education subsidiaries and wholly-owned Woah are early-stage, not established profit engines. Two inactive 59%-owned entities are excluded as immaterial/inactive; their capital commitments are nonetheless visible. The 25% Middle East associate was dissolved and its investment written off; SingaporeAI associate was inactive/unremitted at March 31, with post-year remittance not treated as group revenue. Revenue is not transaction property value, lending volume or developer gross sales.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The moat mechanism is accumulated, continuously refreshed project-level observations, hard-to-rebuild historical comparability and integration into recurring professional research decisions. Management describes 18 years of history,53 cities and 300+clients; its Q1 retention 81% supports repeat relevance but is not independently certified net revenue retention. Historical data is defensible only while collection quality, coverage and client workflow usefulness remain strong. No verified market-share rank, top-client revenue concentration, pricing power cohort or exclusive dataset right was obtained, so monopoly language is inappropriate. Competition includes other research/valuation firms, public records, brokers and customers’ own analytics. AI can lower analysis costs yet also lower switching costs and requires expensive data engineering. Crisil, ICRA and Latent View are useful economics comparators, not valuation peers to average: their regulated ratings/global research, risk platforms and labor-based analytics have different scale, geography, concentration and capital structures. No precise contemporaneous peer P/E was authenticated; those multiples remain ND rather than invented.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Choose comparable FY2023–FY2026 group operating revenue before scoring: ₹29.0538 cr to₹46.8273 cr, CAGR17.25%, anchor 7 with no trajectory uplift. The displayed FY2021–FY2026 CAGR21.06% is explicitly scope-mixed because FY2021 excludes Propedge and FY2022 includes only its postacquisition period. FY23 onward subscription CAGR is 15.38%; FY26 subscriptions rise 21.82% while valuation falls 17.53%, leaving group growth 5.48%, not the 6.22% total-income growth that includes treasury income. Annual additions and endpoints are embedded. No material revenue acquisition in the chosen window is identified, but no perfect price/volume/client bridge is disclosed, so call this substantially comparable operating growth rather than proven unit-level organic growth. Q1FY27 revenues rebound 24.93%, yet PBT grows 7.78%; research declines 49.3% despite an unsigned positive percentage label. One quarter does not justify annualizing or cherry-picking a new window.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The base bottom-up path grows the parent subscription/research revenue pool 12% annually and valuation 8%, keeps parent operating margin 45% before incremental platform staff and valuation margin 5%, then deducts the new₹5.61 cr annual team cost with 5% annual escalation. This is a disclosed-cost overlay, not invented client count times invented ARPU; all new AI revenue must arrive through those existing revenue pools. A half/full/1.5 x incremental-staff sensitivity handles possible overlap with existing personnel. Hardware₹1.072 cr is one-time at modeled deployment, while continuing cash capex 2.5% of revenue maintains the assets. Base cash taxes 25%, operating funding target 0% sales and a₹5 cr cash reserve make the path explicit. Customer advances make historical capital intensity unusually low, but renewed advance receipts also carry delivery obligations. Growth quality is supported by renewal demand and high historical incremental gross operating-asset return; it is tempered by staffing payback, cyclical valuation demand and expense visibility. No terminal value or funding is granted to the proposed₹7 cr Tech investment, and no subsidy is assumed.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Capital allocation has built a large treasury cushion but also AIF/quoted-equity exposure, new subsidiaries and a disputed valuation business. The clean FY26 main opinions and actual parent IFC annexure are material positive evidence; subsidiaries’ exemption prevents a whole-group IFC assurance claim. Historical FY24 audit trail covered May 11 onward and FY25 notes missing earlier preservation; later clean years do not retroactively cure that gap. FY23 subsidiary ESIC arrear₹19,402 was paid May 29,2023, not left as a current default. The tiny 75.0026% promoter MPS excess is disclosed in audit emphasis; September 72.26% postissue holding cures the arithmetic while regulatory closure is not established. Family remuneration/rent and related consultancy are disclosed and need arm’s-length monitoring, not automatic fraud labels. The company alleges former Propedge-director mismanagement/embezzlement and reports proceedings; no guilt is established. A₹1 cr support loan and overdue₹0.0434 cr interest indicate execution/collection stress, not additional consolidated debt. Delivery ledger: IPO2022 technology/retail plans remain partly unspent₹5.5825 cr at FY26; May 2026 HDFC parent proposal closes July 3; new-team spending is funded but monetization unproven; October 8 auditor appointment remains proposed for November 2. HDFC consent rights improve checks but do not replace minority judgment.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 operating revenue₹46.8273 cr plus other income₹7.0163 cr yields total income₹53.8436 cr; normalized core EBIT₹13.9654 cr and D&A₹0.4927 cr give core EBITDA₹14.4581 cr. Group PAT₹15.6734 cr differs from owners PAT₹15.6907 cr; value ordinary holders using attributable profits and postissue shares, not the published EPS blindly. FY25 originalAR25 EPS12.30 reconciles owners PAT, whileAR26 comparative 11.14 and note 12.67 use inconsistent presentation/numerators. Core statements reconcile, making this bounded, not an automatic material-reliability Hold. Four-year CFO/PAT63.01% is depressed by investing classification of treasury interest/dividends; adding those gross receipts to CFO, which already bears total cash taxes, gives 101.69%. Do not deduct tax again or use the adjusted ratio as evidence of operating sales growth. FY22 OFS liability inflow₹12.5582 cr is removed for a diagnostic cash series; FY23 financing settlement is not an operating penalty. Bad debts and provisions remain operating costs. Net capital is negative and decreasing; net incrementalROIC is NM, while the gross operating-asset return proxy 39.15% over FY23–26 gives a conservative public-data cross-check. Unfunded gratuity₹1.6913 cr is included in operating capital, not subtracted from model cash a second time. Rent is expensed underAS19; lease commitment₹0.3746 cr withinone year,₹1.7588 cr 1–5 years and₹0.3952 cr thereafter is not added as capitalized lease debt. Actual corporate bank maturity buckets, restricted proceeds, AIF locks and potential₹11.8 cr capital commitments matter more than the headlinecash balance.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Use a consistent sum of attributable operating earnings value and retained cash: parent NOPAT plus 80% of Propedge NOPAT at 8 x/12 x/16 x bear/base/bull, excluding treasury income from the earnings multiple. Opening group cash is reduced once for minority book interest and IPO earmark; long deposits remain segregated until assumed March 2028 release. Base assumes the shorter deposits can be redeemed before the artificial June commitment payment without principal haircut; no bank-specific early-redemption penalty is verified and the below-reported treasury yield allows ordinary interest friction. An all-deposit-access-delay diagnostic separately suppresses returns when that conservative combined timing stress creates a cash gap; it is not an actual default finding. Gross July 3 equity proceeds enter a restricted bucket, with an explicit₹0.10 cr issue-fee assumption; eligible staff/hardware/general uses reduce that bucket once, while IPO proceeds fund assumed eligible technology capex once. The unsplit unspent IPO objects do not authenticate eligibility of all group capex; a separate zero-IPO-use sensitivity keeps the entire remainder restricted and out of terminal surplus. Unspent earmarks are excluded from terminal surplus. Preentry operating profits are conservatively zero-credited while issue receipt, deployment and a full₹11.8 cr zero-recovery commitment stress are dated. An estimated₹0.3773 cr remaining AIF call (disclosed total commitments₹4.09 cr less₹3.7127 cr carrying investment, pool-comparability assumption) is paid before entry without crediting extra terminal recovery; a larger call remains a monitoring risk. Full group capex/working-capital uses are borne by owners conservatively; NOPAT and D&A use attributable revenue. No fresh financing or rescue is assumed. Treasury cash returns 2.5%/3.5%/4% after tax are separate from operating NOPAT, and no dividends are double-counted. Terminal₹5 cr reserve is retained; investment book cost and accrued interest recoveries are haircut by case, not market-valued from a stale March share price. At₹187 market cap is₹203.45 cr and postissue trailing ownersP/E12.97 x, but those earnings precede full new staff cost. Base 15% hurdle entry₹149.98,12% entry₹171.16,18% entry₹131.86; none is an executable price claim. Reverse growth for 15% is 17.36% at fixedbase margins, staff and 12 x exit, with funded bracket and residual verified. Complete dated ledgers and 27 valuation/36 funding sensitivity rows are embedded.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is not imminent insolvency. It is a profitable niche data franchise funding a large, recurring product team without proportional renewals or pricing, while valuation services remain weak and treasury capital is trapped or poorly allocated. Bear parent growth 4%, valuation−3%, parent margin 38% before new staff, valuation margin−3%, staff 1.2 x budget and 8 x exit produce terminal₹119.91 and conditionalIRR-8.51%. The share price can lose roughly 36% over five years despite a surviving company. Gross fees are not guaranteed repeat ARR; customer retention 81% still permits economically meaningful churn. Bank maturities, disputed-subsidiary support, fund commitments and bad debts can reduce realizable asset backing; illiquid SME lots can magnify exit loss. Funding stresses delay all long-deposit release, raise working-capital/capex needs and vary cash reserve 0/5/10 cr. These tests remain financed in the chosen grid, evidence of a real cushion rather than proof that every conceivable loss is safe. The separate all-deposit-access-delay diagnostic fails the artificial early commitment payment and therefore suppresses its returns, highlighting bank access and actual commitment dates as essential conditions. The thesis-break variable is recurring operating profit after new staffing and credit losses, monitored with subscription renewal/collection quality. An actual adverse legal judgment, withheld deposits or undisclosed support exposure would require new gate review.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold prices over five years require approximately 37.97% and 58.50% annual equity appreciation, far above the funded base return and above the modeled bull. No requested multibagger target justifies forcing optimistic growth. An illustrative operating-scale test holds terminal cash at the base estimate and exit operating NOPAT multiple 12 x: reaching 5 x/10 x would require substantially higher attributable core profit than today after continuing payroll, tax and reinvestment. The precise required profit and reverse parent growth are embedded as diagnostic scale tests. This is not a promise of future margin, a TAM-based forecast or a plan to issue repeated equity without dilution. A data franchise can scale rapidly, but the existing audited trajectory,81% management retention, valuation-service mix and unproven new products do not establish either outcome.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track nine actionable items: (1) subscription revenue FY26₹29.006 cr and 21.82% growth, flag two consecutive periods below 10%; (2) management retention 81%, obtain denominator/net revenue retention and flag below 75%; (3) parent operating margin after incrementalstaff, compare actual cost to₹5.61 cr annual budget and flag sustained cost growth above recurring fees; (4) valuation revenue FY26₹16.4132 cr, require sustained positive cash profits after rebound rather than revenue alone; (5) net receivables₹6.9187 cr,unbilled₹2.4722 cr and doubtful reserve₹1.1216 cr, flag growth faster than sales or renewed ageing; (6) deferred income₹9.2507 cr, reconcile advance cash with service delivery and renewal; (7) actual restricted proceeds/deposit maturities and dormant₹11.8 cr commitments, obtain legal cancellation or payable schedule; (8) Propedge proceedings/loan interest and auditor appointment, distinguish filed events from management intent; (9) current 600-share lot, fresh trade/spread and complete 20/60session observations before any liquidity score. Refresh after next filed half-year/full-year results or a material governance/funding event, not after each price tick. No automation or trading is authorized by this plan.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: Insufficient evidence for a current investment setup; research watchlist with investable but not exceptional business quality. BQS6.6 and GQS6.9 remain eligible for their separate business/growth comparisons. IAS is NS, excluded from price-dependent rankings becauseL is NS and the quote is stale; mathematical bounds are not a filled matrix cell. Even the conditional base at₹187 misses the 15% hurdle. The compounder designation fails BQS≥8 and governance≥7, irrespective of the low headlineP/E. Action category is research priority/watchlist, not an instruction to buy, reduce or exit an unknown portfolio. A lower fresh price near or below the funded 15% reference₹149.98 would improve modeled returns but would not itself cure tradability or governance conditions. Conversely, verified high renewal quality and profitable platform delivery could justify revised operating assumptions. Do not use unknown tax basis, position weight or user risk tolerance to invent a personalized trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Source register ties each fact to official annual reports, full main/audit-annexure pages, company corporate actions, primary shareholding and authenticated NSEpayloads. Financials are₹thousand converted once to₹crore by dividing 10000; share/value conversions use₹10 million percr. IndianGAAP and scope changes are explicit. October 21 material Propedge filing is after cutoff and has no evidentiary effect on the October 20 verdict. Key open questions are audited renewal/cohort pricing and client concentration, exact overlap of new staffing with the existing cost base, subsidiary dispute outcome, capital commitment cancellation, undrawn Tech funding terms, detailed AIF calls, bank encumbrance/maturity eligibility, and complete tradability data. Model assumptions are not audited fact: growth/margins,25% tax, recurringstaff ramp, reserve₹5 cr, full zero-recovery commitment stress, long deposit release, investment haircuts and exit multiples all remain explicit and sensitivity-tested.

evidence.claim: P.E. Analytics Limited, NSE PROPEQUITY, ISIN INE0KN801013, is an SME-listed data/research and property-valuation group. October 19 active SM security row verifies 600-share lot and 10,879,904 shares.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: The master has alternate inactive/eligibility series; those are not separate companies or proof of a live executable quote.

evidence.claim: FY26 subscription fees were ₹29.0060 cr, research ₹1.4081 cr and valuation services ₹16.4132 cr. Group operating revenue ₹46.8273 cr rose 5.48%, while subscription grew 21.82% and valuation fell 17.53%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Service-line figures are not audited segment operating-profit disclosures; avoid invented margins or equating all revenue with recurring subscription ARR.

evidence.claim: The subscription database tracks primary real-estate projects and historical observations, with management describing 300+ clients,53 cities,70,000developers and 195,000projects; Q1FY27 retention is 81%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Customer count and retention are management KPIs without cohort denominator, gross/net revenue retention, ARPU or independently audited renewal economics.

evidence.claim: FY26 unearned revenue increased to ₹9.2507 cr from ₹6.8620 cr; annual subscriptions vary by city/vertical and partly fund operations in advance.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Deferred income is a service obligation, not free distributable cash or incremental backlog valued a second time.

evidence.claim: Consolidated FY26 main opinion, parent CARO, and actual parent IFC annexure are unmodified; audit-trail reporting is positive. Subsidiaries are exempt from IFC reporting.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Do not claim group-wide tested IFC. Earlier FY24 trail began May 11,2023 and FY25 preserves that historical gap; clean later reporting does not erase it.

evidence.claim: FY26 audit emphasis identifies promoter 75.0026% versus 75% MPS limit. September 30 primary shareholding reports 72.26%,10,879,904 shares and no promoter pledges/encumbrance.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Dilution mathematically cures the ownership percentage by cutoff; this does not excuse the earlier compliance lapse or establish regulator closure.

evidence.claim: The company alleges financial mismanagement and embezzlement by a former Propedge director and reports legal proceedings plus parent support loan ₹1 cr; loan interest overdue₹0.0434 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Allegation is not adjudicated guilt. Loan is intragroup and eliminated in group cash/debt; the October 21 filing is excluded from cutoff analysis.

evidence.claim: FY26 gross bank cash/deposits₹96.174 cr comprises current-account cash₹6.8584 cr,3–12month deposits₹42.1966 cr and longer deposits₹47.119 cr. IPO earmark remains₹5.5825 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Not all deposits are immediately unrestricted. Note 41 arithmetic appears to subtract issue expense twice; retain the larger reported earmark rather than freeing the discrepancy.

evidence.claim: Actual July 3 allotment raised₹7.99578 cr gross for 397,800 shares at₹201. Uses include 59-person annual payroll₹5.61 cr, hardware₹1.072 cr and general purposes₹1.3138 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Recurring staff must persist after the issue budget year. Neither projected platform revenue nor separate proposed₹7 cr Tech funding is treated as achieved.

evidence.claim: Two inactive 59%-owned subsidiaries carry aggregate subscribed capital commitments₹11.8 cr despite a proposed strikeoff. Group investments include₹3.7127 cr AIF funds and₹3.5404 cr quoted equities at book cost.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Subscription can merely move cash within the group; the full zero-recovery outflow is a deliberately conservative funding stress, not a proven external liability already paid.

evidence.claim: FY23–26 reported CFO₹32.2819 cr divided by same-scope group PAT₹51.2346 cr is 63.01%. Adding gross investing-classified interest/dividend cash after the already-paid total taxes gives₹52.1016 cr and 101.69%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: This corrects classification, not business quality: treasury income remains excluded from operating multiples and bad-debt expense remains recurring.

evidence.claim: FY22 CFO₹20.5457 cr includes₹12.5582 cr OFS proceeds payable to the promoter. The subsequent FY23 repayment is financing cashflow.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Do not score FY22 as a huge operating-cash windfall or subtract its repayment from later operating cash twice.

evidence.claim: FY26 receivables net₹6.9187 cr, doubtful reserve₹1.1216 cr and unbilled₹2.4722 cr coexist with₹0.4337 cr written-off debts and₹0.3182 cr new doubtful provision.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Good receivables are under one year, positive counterevidence; neither age bucket proves collection nor bad debts warrant a perpetual one-off addback.

evidence.claim: Group normalized operating EBIT excludes all other income: FY26₹13.9654 cr versus total PBT₹20.9817 cr. Owners PAT₹15.6907 cr differs from group PAT₹15.6734 cr owing to minority loss.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: A low reported P/E incorporates treasury earnings and predates the announced staffing ramp. FY25 displayed EPS variants reconcile to different numerators, not different cash.

evidence.claim: Net operating invested capital FY23−₹0.4221 cr to FY26−₹2.9975 cr declines as customer/operating funding grows; NOPAT rises₹2.1894 cr. Gross operating assets rise₹5.5930 cr, giving 39.15% incremental profit/gross-asset proxy.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Net incremental ROIC is NM with declining/negative capital, not a negative economic return. FY23–24 gross-asset return was only 8.75%, so returns are uneven.

evidence.claim: Q1FY27 reported operating revenue₹13.3066 cr rose 24.93%; PBT₹5.477 cr rose 7.78%. Subscription growth 22.8%, research decline 49.3%, valuation rebound 39.9%.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Quarter is unaudited management presentation, not audited cashflow. PBT grows slower than sales during staff/cost ramp; do not annualize the best quarter.

evidence.claim: Only 29 of 60 authenticated calendar sessions have issuer trade rows; seven of 20 recent sessions have rows. Last observed official trade is₹187 on October 9,1,200 shares,two trades.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: 31 absent rows are missing observations, not measured zero trades; no current full-window ADTV or October 19 executable quote can be claimed.

evidence.claim: One 600-share lot costs₹112,200 at the stale reference. Four lots cost₹448,800; five cost₹561,000. Observed-only median volume 1,800 supports zero whole lots at 2%,5% or 10% participation.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Observed-only median turnover and hypothetical fractional days cannot restore missing full-window liquidity evidence.

evidence.claim: HDFC minority consent rights cover specified extraordinary matters and some related-party dealings; fallaway is tied to retaining at least half allotted shares.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Institutional participation supports external scrutiny, not a blanket valuation endorsement or proof every related-party transaction is favorable.

evidence.claim: Related-party rent and remuneration are disclosed: Samir remuneration₹0.5678 cr,Vaishali₹0.3646 cr,Pooja₹0.3378 cr; Topaz rent₹0.3720 cr and Samir rent₹0.0795 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Disclosed family transactions require arm’s-length monitoring; amounts alone do not establish diversion. Rent remains in recurring operating margins.

evidence.claim: October 8 board proposes auditor reappointment at November 2 EGM. Annual CARO says no auditor resignation during FY26.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Do not infer misconduct, resignation or a completed shareholder approval from a proposal.

evidence.claim: Crisil research/analytics, ICRA research/analytics and Latent View analytics illustrate recurring information versus labor-service economics.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: No peer is a pure Indian real-estate dataset SME. Size, regulation, currency, client concentration and services mix prevent mechanical multiple transfer.

summary: P.E. Analytics is a cash-rich real-estate information business with a meaningful recurring subscription franchise, alongside a weaker and more cyclical valuation-services subsidiary. The decisive strength is data renewal revenue financed partly by customer advances; the decisive risk is that announced platform expansion creates recurring payroll before its revenues are proven. This is an asset-light growth/value watchlist thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder designation. At the authenticated but stale October 9 reference of ₹187, the funded base model returns 10.04%, below the 15% hurdle, versus -8.51% bear and 23.11% bull. The base 15% hurdle reference is ₹149.98, not a live buy order. BQS 6.6 and GQS 6.9 are scoreable; IAS stays NS because full-window liquidity is not established. Better returns require profitable adoption of the new team, a lower executable price, or stronger evidenced growth, not counting proposed funding as cash.
